newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Pharmos sees FDA approval in 3rd quarter.
newsitem.headline: Pharmos sees FDA approval in 3rd quarter.

text.p: Israel's Pharmos said on Thursday it expected U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to approve its eye treatment Lotemax in the third quarter of this year.

"Our first approval is very important. It will give us recognition and it will touch off the the flow of revenues from our partner Bausch & Lomb," Pharmos chairman Haim Aviv told Reuters after speaking to traders and analysts in Tel Aviv.
Bausch & Lomb will be responsible for the worldwide marketing of Pharmos' Lotemax, which the company said treats eye inflammations without the side effects of other steroid medications.
Aviv said he expected the FDA to approve the drug during the third quarter of this year.
In December, Bausch & Lomb also acquired a stake in the company buying $2 million worth of common stock. The company has also helped finance the drug's development.
Aviv said Lotemax was the first of three opthalmic drugs the company had developed using loteprednol etabonate, a site-specific steroid.

A second medication used for treating seasonal allergies was expected to get FDA approval early next year, he said. The company is also developing a drug for neurology disorders and a cancer treatment

Profits, however, will not kick in until 1998, according to a report by Jesup and Lamont Securities Corp published last November. It forecast revenues of $1 million this year, rising to $17 million in 1998.
The report said earnings would only begin in 1998 -- Pharmos' first full year of sales -- and would reach $0.04 per share. It estimated they would climb to $0.25 a share in 1999.
Shares in Pharmos, a Floria-based company that conducts most of its operations in Israel, trade at about $1.50 on the Nasdaq, close to the bottom end of their 52-week range.
"Right now, before they're showing signs of any sales, an agreement with Bausch & Lomb is not going to make them profitable," said Haim Hoffman, who works in the securities division of Bank Leumi.
"But once they make their first breakthrough the company shares can reach $20 in three months," he said.
